triggers: A proposal to tidy a screen with a modal, drawer, accordion, tabs, or hidden details.
principles.exceptions: Reject universal single-open accordions, bans on scrolling dialogs, or claims that drawers always preserve context; compare actual content, task, and platform behavior.

verification.question: Can people reveal detail, retain the initiating object or section, compare necessary facts, and return without losing task position?

principles.title: Preserve the meaning of destinations, view switches, and Back

source.heading: TD-27 — Preserve the meaning of destinations, view switches, and Back

triggers: Tabs used for commands, peer-view switching, deep drilldown, or a single-page implementation with surprising Back behavior.
principles.exceptions: Top-only tabs, fixed tab counts, first-tab defaults, and rejection of primary tab navigation are not current platform requirements. Historical usage does not prove universal comprehension.

verification.question: Can people predict whether a control changes destination or performs an action, and does actual Back or return restore the promised context?

principles.title: Preserve orientation without letting fixed controls consume the task

source.heading: TD-28 — Preserve orientation without letting fixed controls consume the task

triggers: Long scrolling content, sticky headers, bottom action bars, batch selection, or controls competing with the keyboard and system edges.
principles.exceptions: Neither ubiquitous fixed controls nor a blanket web-bottom-bar ban follows. Check current browser/OS edges, keyboard, safe areas, content space, and access settings in runtime.

verification.question: During scrolling, selection, enlarged text, and keyboard use, are both content and required actions reachable with location and scope intact?

principles.title: Preserve the user's comparison when simplifying a collection

source.heading: TD-29 — Preserve the user's comparison when simplifying a collection

triggers: A wide data table, list/card redesign, narrow viewport, or excessive attributes in a result row.
principles.exceptions: Cards, horizontal table scroll, and transformed records can fit specific tasks. Do not hide material decision facts or infer HTML table semantics from list-like appearance.

verification.question: Can intended users answer the required comparison using visible attributes, then retrieve detail without confusing entities or losing the original set?

principles.title: Make collection previews reveal their extent and alternate routes

source.heading: TD-30 — Make collection previews reveal their extent and alternate routes

triggers: Horizontally scrolling category rows, image-led browsing, truncated collections, or a gesture-only carousel.
principles.exceptions: Carousels may fit exploration but hinder precise finding or comparison. A clipped item alone is neither sufficient accessibility nor mandatory; historical screenshots do not prove current behavior.

verification.question: Can people discover additional items, reach them without swiping, identify individual items, and return to their previous collection context?

principles.title: Investigate the real device, environment, and service assumptions

source.heading: TD-31 — Investigate the real device, environment, and service assumptions

triggers: A mobile brief based on the team's own phones, location-dependent work, connectivity assumptions, or a task performed outside a desk setting.
principles.exceptions: Dated device statistics and technical explanations require current verification. Source recommendations authorize no recruitment or tracking, and coarse or aggregated location is not automatically private.

verification.question: Which task behavior relies on an untested device, environment, network, input, or data assumption, and what observation would resolve it?

principles.title: Carry task rationale into implementation and realistic evaluation

source.heading: TD-32 — Carry task rationale into implementation and realistic evaluation

triggers: Design handoff, a technically polished but brittle flow, claims based on mock-ups, or a release whose behavior diverges from the brief.
principles.exceptions: Do not impose a rigid process or printed measurement templates. A mock-up displayed on a phone supports limited scale inspection, not live hit-region, transition, or usability validation.

verification.question: What was actually checked on which artifact and device, did the changed path preserve task intent, and what still needs runtime or participant evidence?

principles.title: Define experience quality beyond task completion

source.heading: ID-01 — Define experience quality beyond task completion

triggers: Framing a new experience or evaluating an apparently successful conversion.
principles.exceptions: Do not turn broad audience assertions into stereotypes or impose pleasure on serious moments. A minimal interface can retain useful character and expressive detail.

verification.question: Can a successful completion still leave the person confused, excluded, pressured or unsure what happened?

principles.title: Design the exposed conceptual model before the screens

source.heading: ID-02 — Design the exposed conceptual model before the screens

triggers: New navigation, unfamiliar objects, or a feature organized like backend services.
principles.exceptions: A model is a hypothesis, not proof of comprehension. Technical details belong in the interface only when they help a decision.

verification.question: Could a person predict what an object contains, which action changes it, and where the result will appear?

principles.title: Use metaphors as limited bridges and manage their promises

source.heading: ID-03 — Use metaphors as limited bridges and manage their promises

triggers: Wallets, cards, assistants, mascots, or other familiar imagery suggesting unfamiliar behavior.
principles.exceptions: The book acknowledges Cooper’s objections to metaphor; preserve this tension rather than prescribing metaphor everywhere. Decorative imagery need not become a literal operating model.

verification.question: What capability does this representation imply, and does the actual behavior support that expectation?

principles.title: Choose an interaction form by its effort and repair path

source.heading: ID-04 — Choose an interaction form by its effort and repair path

triggers: Considering chat, forms, gestures, direct manipulation or automation for a task.
principles.exceptions: Natural-looking interaction is not inherently easy. A deterministic form can be more efficient than dialogue; unfamiliar gestures may require learning.

verification.question: Can the person recover from a mistaken inference without restarting or learning hidden syntax?

principles.title: Externalize state without inventing item-count limits

source.heading: ID-05 — Externalize state without inventing item-count limits

triggers: Dense summaries, interrupted tasks, multi-step forms or a proposed maximum number of visible options.
principles.exceptions: Visibility has density and attention costs. A visible list is not automatically easy to scan, and repeating every detail everywhere can obscure priorities.

verification.question: After interruption, can the person see where they are, what is retained and what remains to do?

principles.title: Match emotional expression to the moment and repeated use

source.heading: ID-06 — Match emotional expression to the moment and repeated use

triggers: Visual direction, empty states, completion, errors or recurring mascot appearances.
principles.exceptions: The Clippy account does not justify banning all resident mascots. Humor that fits browsing may trivialize uncertainty or financial loss. Owner taste and source examples do not prove the audience feels reassured.

verification.question: Does expression support understanding and the right emotional tone without competing with status, action or recovery?

principles.title: Represent awareness without assuming attention or consent

source.heading: ID-07 — Represent awareness without assuming attention or consent

triggers: Shared status, social features, assistant messages or public participation indicators.
principles.exceptions: Do not introduce social instrumentation merely because it is possible. Workplace or immersive examples do not establish needs in a personal finance app.

verification.question: Could someone mistake a presence or activity cue for availability, agreement or a demand to respond?

principles.title: Select input controls around the answer people already know

source.heading: ID-08 — Select input controls around the answer people already know

triggers: Long pickers, search, forms or replacing typing with recognition controls.
principles.exceptions: Do not infer nationality from location or treat recognition as universally superior. Historical country dropdowns and touch dimensions are not current native specifications.

verification.question: Can a person who knows the answer enter it quickly, while someone uncertain can discover valid choices?

principles.title: Keep meaning available across presentation and access conditions

source.heading: ID-09 — Keep meaning available across presentation and access conditions

triggers: Icon-only actions, unfamiliar gestures, touch feedback or accessibility exploration.
principles.exceptions: Do not generalize the book’s color, target-size or demographic simplifications. Haptics, animation and pictures should not become the sole carrier of an essential message.

verification.question: Can the supported task be understood and completed through the relevant access route, and which needs remain untested?

principles.title: Fit evidence collection to the question and keep methods distinguishable

source.heading: ID-10 — Fit evidence collection to the question and keep methods distinguishable

triggers: Research planning, source synthesis or a claim supported by several different observations.
principles.exceptions: There is no universally sufficient interview or app count. Triangulation can reveal disagreement rather than remove it. Source sampling and legal/consent simplifications are not adopted.

verification.question: Does each piece of evidence answer the claim it is being used to support?

principles.title: Make research prompts and response controls valid for the claim

source.heading: ID-11 — Make research prompts and response controls valid for the claim

triggers: Preparing a survey, interview, preference question or structured visual comparison.
principles.exceptions: Closed choices are useful when well scoped but cannot establish omitted explanations. Do not generalize book response-rate thresholds or treat all checkbox responses as independent people.

verification.question: Could a reasonable answer be missing, forced into two ranges, or changed by the way the question is phrased?

principles.title: Preserve evidence units, counterexamples and uncertainty during analysis

source.heading: ID-12 — Preserve evidence units, counterexamples and uncertainty during analysis

triggers: Counts, ratings, analytics, coded observations or claims of visual improvement.
principles.exceptions: The source’s casual recommendation to remove outliers and its oversimplified statistics are not adopted. Agreement between coders does not establish truth, and a rating difference does not quantify objective beauty.

verification.question: Would the conclusion change if an unusual case, missing response or alternative explanation were retained?

principles.title: Design summaries and visualizations for a particular question

source.heading: ID-13 — Design summaries and visualizations for a particular question

triggers: Dashboards, scores, comparisons or dense financial summaries.
principles.exceptions: Less data is not universally better; neither is more charting. Attractive illustrative data does not establish accuracy or meaningful scoring. Avoid misleading scales and visual encodings.

verification.question: Can the intended person tell what this value covers, why it matters now, and what to do with it?

principles.title: Treat inferred emotion and opaque scores as uncertain representations

source.heading: ID-14 — Treat inferred emotion and opaque scores as uncertain representations

triggers: Emotion detection, personalized recommendations, tracking or an interface that appears to know how someone feels.
principles.exceptions: A sentiment label or sensor output is not a direct reading of felt experience. Legal, fairness and liability simplifications in this book are excluded; current applicable requirements need independent verification.

verification.question: Can the person understand and challenge the consequential inference without being shamed or misled?

principles.title: Specify requirements as behavior, data quality and use context

source.heading: ID-15 — Specify requirements as behavior, data quality and use context

triggers: A screen brief, implementation contract or flow that seems complete only in the happy path.
principles.exceptions: Do not invent research personas or quotes. Requirements need enough detail for the decision, not exhaustive paperwork; genuine findings may revise them.

verification.question: Which data or contextual assumption would make the apparently correct screen fail its real task?

principles.title: Trace the journey outside the interface and through alternate outcomes

source.heading: ID-16 — Trace the journey outside the interface and through alternate outcomes

triggers: Multi-screen work, interrupted setup or an experience whose success depends on events before and after the app.
principles.exceptions: Do not mistake a polished journey map for evidence or require a large workshop artifact for a small change. A map and a wireflow answer related but different questions.

verification.question: What happens immediately before entry, after completion and when the intended sequence is interrupted?

principles.title: Choose prototype fidelity along the dimensions the question requires

source.heading: ID-17 — Choose prototype fidelity along the dimensions the question requires

triggers: Deciding whether to sketch, render, build natively or simulate an external service.
principles.exceptions: A narrow prototype is legitimate if claims stay narrow. High visual fidelity does not establish task reliability, and prototype success does not make code production-ready.

verification.question: Which claim can this artifact actually establish, and what remains fake or untested?

principles.title: Use negative scenarios to test a concept’s social and emotional cost

source.heading: ID-18 — Use negative scenarios to test a concept’s social and emotional cost

triggers: Promising new concepts, mascots, automation or features justified only by an optimistic story.
principles.exceptions: These are design probes, not fabricated participant testimony or predictions of frequency. Avoid treating every speculative concern as a proven defect.

verification.question: Under what plausible circumstance would the same delightful feature become intrusive, embarrassing or confusing?

principles.title: Treat pattern popularity as a search clue rather than a verdict

source.heading: ID-19 — Treat pattern popularity as a search clue rather than a verdict

triggers: Mobbin references, design-system extensions or a request to copy a familiar screen.
principles.exceptions: One app’s distinctive appearance is not a universal prescription, and several apps repeating a pattern are not independent usability studies. Historical implementation examples require current platform checks.

verification.question: What problem does this pattern solve here, and which costs or missing states does the reference leave unresolved?

principles.title: Carry research into delivery without turning it into ceremony

source.heading: ID-20 — Carry research into delivery without turning it into ceremony

triggers: Handoffs, subagents, long-running implementation or a design library growing faster than its use.
principles.exceptions: This is our implementation of the book’s collaboration concern, not a prescribed sprint length, mandatory team structure or extra approval gate. Routine approved edits remain small.

verification.question: Can the implementer and reviewer find the consequential reason and criterion at the moment they need it?

principles.title: Preserve useful strengths while resolving conflicts

source.heading: ID-21 — Preserve useful strengths while resolving conflicts

triggers: Critique, redesign or synthesis across books with different emphases.
principles.exceptions: A consistent visual system can deliberately differentiate consequential actions. Neither minimalism nor expressiveness independently guarantees quality.

verification.question: Which existing strength could this improvement damage, and what evidence justifies the tradeoff?

principles.title: Keep cultural and access context explicit when extending a product

source.heading: ID-22 — Keep cultural and access context explicit when extending a product

triggers: Localization, new audiences, alternative inputs or transferring a successful example to another context.
principles.exceptions: Do not replace evidence with national or demographic stereotypes. This does not require supporting every device or undertaking a new field study for every edit.

verification.question: Which contextual assumption is least supported for the intended audience, and how does the design cope if it is wrong?

principles.title: Match evaluation claims to evidence and setting

source.heading: ID-23 — Match evaluation claims to evidence and setting

triggers: Planning an improvement comparison or describing what a prototype established.
principles.exceptions: A narrow check can be useful without generalizing. A simulator run does not establish hand comfort in ordinary mobile use; artificiality alone does not invalidate a scoped result.

verification.question: Does the evidence measure the claimed improvement, and what consequential question remains unanswered?

principles.title: Use formative findings to change and recheck the design

source.heading: ID-24 — Use formative findings to change and recheck the design

triggers: Early visual alternatives, evolving flows or pilot findings.
principles.exceptions: Do not require a new approval checkpoint for every reversible change or generalize local feedback to all users.

verification.question: Which decision changed or gained support, and was the revised path exercised?

principles.title: Keep comparisons matched and samples proportionate to the question

source.heading: ID-25 — Keep comparisons matched and samples proportionate to the question

triggers: Baseline-versus-redesign tasks, numeric claims or choosing an evaluation sample.
A/B testing or a baseline comparison changes several variables at once.
principles.exceptions: Do not adopt a universal five-person rule or the source’s misleading p-value explanation. Seek suitable statistical expertise for inferential claims. Script correctness, preference and lived experience remain different outcomes.

verification.question: What exactly improved, for whom, under which conditions and with which uncertainty?

principles.title: Scope actual participant involvement and interpret traces with context

source.heading: ID-26 — Scope actual participant involvement and interpret traces with context

triggers: Authorized recruitment, recording, interviews, analytics or interpreting online behavior.
principles.exceptions: This does not authorize recruitment or tracking, and it does not add a consent ceremony to a local fixture inspection. Current applicable requirements supersede dated legal descriptions.

verification.question: Were people and data treated as agreed, and could the apparent behavior have another contextual explanation?

principles.title: Define analytics before interpreting success or failure

source.heading: ID-27 — Define analytics before interpreting success or failure

triggers: Drop-off, long sessions, engagement differences or a proposed analytics-based improvement claim.
principles.exceptions: No automatic tracking installation is authorized. Historical product instructions, bounce-rate bands and market shares are not current requirements or quality thresholds. Anonymization alone does not settle all ethical concerns.

verification.question: What human goal does this metric represent, what is its denominator, and what else could produce the observed pattern?

principles.title: Explain design decisions and component usage

source.heading: PU-01 — Explain design decisions and component usage

triggers: Creating a visual system, extending components, or reconciling inconsistent screens.
principles.exceptions: The book’s sample palette, shadow count, radii, and left-alignment conventions describe its own system. They are not requirements for every product. Reuse native controls and approved project decisions where they fit.

verification.question: Can another implementer choose and populate this component appropriately, including its disabled, pressed, focus, and error behavior?

principles.title: Simplify without deleting necessary information

source.heading: PU-02 — Simplify without deleting necessary information

triggers: A sparse screen is difficult to understand, or decoration and repeated content compete with the task.
principles.exceptions: A decorative element can establish character or delight. The book explicitly permits such purposes; it does not justify a blanket ban on gradients, rounded cards, illustration, or mascots. Important terms must not be hidden merely to tidy a financial screen.

verification.question: After simplification, can someone still identify the current state, main task, actionable elements, and any decision-changing information?

principles.title: Reduce choice effort without manufacturing a preferred answer

source.heading: PU-03 — Reduce choice effort without manufacturing a preferred answer

triggers: A long list, comparison, onboarding sequence, or menu demands substantial search and decision work.
principles.exceptions: More steps can improve comprehension or make recovery harder. A recommendation must not invent popularity, conceal costs, or bias an equally valid choice toward the business. The book’s illustrative cost arithmetic is not a validated universal metric.

verification.question: What information must be found, remembered, or re-entered, and is the suggested option justified for this person’s task?

principles.title: Check current contrast requirements and actual legibility

source.heading: PU-04 — Check current contrast requirements and actual legibility

triggers: Selecting text, control, or state colors; inspecting light and dark appearances.
APCA, WCAG, contrast compliance or small-text legibility is disputed.
principles.exceptions: Dated correction verified 2026-10-21: the W3C WCAG3 Working Draft dated2026-09-10 says its contrast algorithm is not yet determined and draft publication is not endorsement. APCA is supplemental, not a substitute for WCAG2.2 web conformance. Native iOS follows current Apple accessibility guidance and the project’s requirements. The book’s blanket concern about pure black on white is not adopted as a universal ban; do not reduce contrast automatically.

verification.question: Is every contrast claim tied to the applicable standard and measured rendered colors, and does small or thin text remain readable in the supported appearance?

principles.title: Give color a stable role and a second channel for meaning

source.heading: PU-05 — Give color a stable role and a second channel for meaning

triggers: Brand colors, status badges, links, selected items, or warnings appear in the same experience.
principles.exceptions: A single brand color is a useful starting constraint, not a ban on multicolor brands or mascots. Color associations vary culturally. Static colored content need not be prohibited if it cannot reasonably be mistaken for a control. The p85 color-blindness comparison removes an error label in one grayscale image; it is not a controlled color-only demonstration.

verification.question: Can important state be understood without hue, and can someone distinguish an action from decorative or informational color?

principles.title: Test semantic colors across layers and interaction states

source.heading: PU-06 — Test semantic colors across layers and interaction states

triggers: A design system introduces dark mode, layered surfaces, tinted cards, or translucent fills.
principles.exceptions: The author’s HSB recipe, five-color examples, and overlay percentages are construction methods, not guarantees of accessible contrast. Opaque fills can be more predictable. Dark mode is not automatically more comfortable for every person. Native materials and states should follow platform behavior.

verification.question: Does the same semantic role remain distinguishable and legible on every actual surface and in every relevant state?

principles.title: Use imagery coherently without obscuring content or misrepresenting it

source.heading: PU-07 — Use imagery coherently without obscuring content or misrepresenting it

triggers: Choosing illustrations, photos, mascots, or text overlays as part of a direction.
principles.exceptions: Image warmth is an optional art-direction choice, not a universal rule. Do not recolor images when fidelity is material. A fixed50% overlay cannot guarantee contrast. The rule of thirds is a composition option, not a proven universal attention map.

verification.question: Does this image contribute to the intended experience, and can the message and action still be read on the actual crop at supported sizes?

principles.title: Make grouping and appearance describe ownership and behavior

source.heading: PU-08 — Make grouping and appearance describe ownership and behavior

triggers: Cards, rows, captions, icons, or badges seem attached to the wrong content or suggest nonexistent interactions.
principles.exceptions: Container borders are one solution, not a requirement to put every section into a card. A decorative icon can remain expressive if its treatment does not imply a tappable button. Similarity sometimes intentionally denotes a shared category rather than identical behavior.

verification.question: Can a viewer tell which explanation or action belongs to which item, and does any static element look tappable?

principles.title: Rank decision content before assigning visual emphasis

source.heading: PU-09 — Rank decision content before assigning visual emphasis

triggers: Designing a screen composition or correcting competition among values, actions, illustrations, and metadata.
Visual hierarchy, salience or the primary content competes with metadata.
principles.exceptions: The largest or brightest element need not always be the call to action. Material costs, risk, deadlines, or eligibility may deserve prominence before commitment. A blur check reveals salience; it does not prove comprehension, accessibility, or emotional success.

verification.question: What attracts attention first, second, and third, and does that order support an informed decision in this scenario?

principles.title: Use spacing and alignment to express relationships

source.heading: PU-10 — Use spacing and alignment to express relationships

triggers: A screen is evenly spaced but its sections still feel disconnected or difficult to scan.
principles.exceptions: An8-point grid, twelve web columns, and four mobile columns are optional frameworks. Do not force every relationship into one numerical gap. Leading alignment depends on writing direction; numeric comparison may use a shared trailing or decimal alignment. The p191 explanation conflates linear2x scale with four physical pixels of area; do not adopt that unit conversion.

verification.question: Are within-group gaps visibly smaller than the relevant between-group gaps, and do related labels and values share intentional alignment?

principles.title: Preserve meaningful distinctions when content grows

source.heading: PU-11 — Preserve meaningful distinctions when content grows

triggers: Long account names, large balances, localization, or text scaling stress the layout.
Dynamic Type, localization or truncation hides distinguishing information.
principles.exceptions: Shrinking text is not a general solution and must not defeat Dynamic Type or legibility. Middle truncation only helps when the surviving parts are meaningful. Do not abbreviate precise financial amounts solely for visual neatness.

verification.question: Can users still distinguish every relevant item and read the full decision-critical information with long content and enlarged text?

principles.title: Choose typography for both legibility and character

source.heading: PU-12 — Choose typography for both legibility and character

triggers: Starting an art direction or extending a project’s type system.
principles.exceptions: A single sans-serif family and two weights are beginner-friendly defaults, not bans on serif display faces or native semantic weights. The mood panels at238 also change imagery, color, and shape, so they cannot isolate a font-only emotional effect. Assess a complete direction and identify which variables changed.

verification.question: Does the type support the intended character without compromising glyph distinction, language coverage, small labels, or numeric comparison?

principles.title: Tune type scale, leading, and line length together

source.heading: PU-13 — Tune type scale, leading, and line length together

triggers: Text hierarchy is weak, paragraphs are tiring, or headings feel detached from their content.
principles.exceptions: The book’s pixel sizes, ratios, character counts, and leading ranges are starting heuristics, not universal thresholds or substitutes for native text styles. Avoid overriding a font’s spacing without inspection. Justification and center alignment have contextual uses; writing direction and script matter.

verification.question: Can readers follow lines, recognize headings, and compare values without the type system disrupting the task at supported sizes?

principles.title: Front-load the message without concealing material details

source.heading: PU-14 — Front-load the message without concealing material details

triggers: Writing headings, onboarding explanations, permission prompts, or a dense financial summary.
principles.exceptions: Fixed sentence lengths, reading-grade targets, and omission of articles or punctuation are editing aids rather than universal rules. A benefit-led permission heading must not bury what data will be stored or shared. Long content can be appropriate when comprehension requires it.

verification.question: Does a scan reveal both the benefit and the material commitment, and has shortening removed any information needed for an informed choice?

principles.title: Use precise labels, stable vocabulary, and meaningful numbers

source.heading: PU-15 — Use precise labels, stable vocabulary, and meaningful numbers

triggers: Naming navigation, links, buttons, statuses, or financial values.
principles.exceptions: Delete and remove may represent different operations and should not be collapsed automatically. My versus your depends on perspective, not an absolute ban. Do not pad text to equal length or abbreviate balances at the expense of meaning. Small uppercase labels are not universally prohibited.

verification.question: Can the label be understood on its own, and do its wording and numeric precision accurately predict the result?

principles.title: Explain failure and offer an honest recovery route

source.heading: PU-16 — Explain failure and offer an honest recovery route

triggers: A payment, lookup, save, or connection fails.
principles.exceptions: The p287 example recommends updating payment details after a failed payment; that advice is appropriate only if the system has evidence that those details are the cause. Do not promise a retry, refund, successful save, or recovered state unless implemented.

verification.question: Can the user understand what happened, what was preserved, and what to do next without being given an invented cause?

principles.title: Use action emphasis without biasing equally valid choices

source.heading: PU-17 — Use action emphasis without biasing equally valid choices

triggers: A screen contains several buttons, repeated row actions, or a consequential choice.
principles.exceptions: Native button roles and styles can express hierarchy differently. Do not turn one-primary-action into a quota or demote cancel and privacy choices to serve conversion. The book’s simplified button contrast wording is not an independent compliance standard.

verification.question: Does the action hierarchy match the user’s task, and are all meaningful alternatives still discoverable and understandable?

principles.title: Explain unavailable actions instead of leaving a silent dead end

source.heading: PU-18 — Explain unavailable actions instead of leaving a silent dead end

triggers: An action is disabled because of missing input, permissions, eligibility, or unavailable capability.
principles.exceptions: Do not enable an unsafe or impossible operation merely to avoid gray UI. A lock icon is ambiguous between permission, privacy, and paid access unless explained. Native disabled semantics remain appropriate in many contexts.

verification.question: Can someone determine why the action is unavailable and how to proceed, including with assistive technology?

principles.title: Keep actions close to their context and make targets dependable

source.heading: PU-19 — Keep actions close to their context and make targets dependable

triggers: Placing form actions, menus, dismiss controls, or dense row controls.
principles.exceptions: The author’s preferred left-aligned actions and bottom placement are not universal iOS requirements; p314 explicitly permits right-aligned dialogs. Book point/pixel and target-size examples must not be copied as current cross-platform thresholds. A large invisible hit area does not always fix a tiny perceived control.

verification.question: Can the intended action be found and activated reliably without accidental neighboring activation or losing the content it affects?

principles.title: Match destructive friction to consequences and provide real undo

source.heading: PU-20 — Match destructive friction to consequences and provide real undo

triggers: Deleting, removing, replacing, or committing a difficult-to-reverse change.
principles.exceptions: The author’s blanket advice against red initial destructive actions is not adopted over native destructive roles. Repeated confirmations can teach automatic dismissal. A checkbox confirmation is one option for high consequence, not a requirement for every deletion.

verification.question: Is the protection proportional to the consequence, and has the recovery been exercised rather than merely drawn?

principles.title: Structure forms around necessary information and logical groups

source.heading: PU-21 — Structure forms around necessary information and logical groups

triggers: Building onboarding, card entry, settings, or another multi-field task.
principles.exceptions: Single-column layout and labels above inputs are useful defaults but not a ban on native forms or compact related fields. The author qualifies marking every required field for familiar or single-question flows. Do not make every question a separate step automatically.

verification.question: Is each field necessary at this point, is completion status clear, and can users correct a previous answer without starting over?

principles.title: Keep labels available and help visible when it is needed

source.heading: PU-22 — Keep labels available and help visible when it is needed

triggers: A person must remember an input’s purpose or discover a formatting requirement.
Placeholder-only labels or keyboard occlusion hide input meaning.
principles.exceptions: A familiar search field may use a compact presentation while retaining an accessible name. Optional elaboration can be disclosed. Native layout may place help differently if it remains discoverable and available; the goal is timely comprehension, not copying a web stack mechanically.

verification.question: While typing or reviewing a filled form, can the user still identify the field, its requirements, and how to correct it?

principles.title: Choose controls for the selection task and commitment model

source.heading: PU-23 — Choose controls for the selection task and commitment model

triggers: Selecting an item from a long set, changing a quantity, or editing a binary setting.
principles.exceptions: A ten-item threshold is not a law. Steppers can be inefficient for large values. Native toggles can participate in a draft form; preserve the actual commit contract instead of enforcing a web checkbox rule. Custom card selection should retain clear semantics and state.

verification.question: Can the intended item be found without prior vocabulary, and is it clear whether a selection is tentative or already applied?

principles.title: Choose validation timing that supports correction

source.heading: PU-24 — Choose validation timing that supports correction

triggers: An input has format, eligibility, cross-field, or server-side constraints.
principles.exceptions: Validation on blur can interrupt focus switching and works poorly for some grouped choices. Immediate checks may be suitable after a known error, but must handle asynchronous stale responses. A green mark must not imply an account or transaction is verified when only syntax was checked.

verification.question: Can users find, understand, correct, and confirm resolution of every error without losing valid work or receiving premature success?

principles.title: Balance users, content, and organizational context

source.heading: IA-01 — Balance users, content, and organizational context

triggers: Defining navigation, restructuring a content-rich product, or deciding whether a reference app's architecture fits.
principles.exceptions: This is a lens for the current decision, not a mandatory discovery phase for every change. User goals remain central, but an architecture whose metadata nobody can maintain will fail. Do not copy a competitor's structure or expose an internal org chart merely because it is convenient for the organization.

verification.question: Can the proposed grouping be explained in terms of actual user needs, content properties and feasible upkeep? What changes when the collection grows or ownership is distributed?

principles.title: Match finding support and success criteria to the information need

source.heading: IA-02 — Match finding support and success criteria to the information need

triggers: Designing a directory, catalog, help center, research tool, recommendations or saved-item experience.
principles.exceptions: These are useful recurring needs, not exhaustive or fixed user types. A single person can switch needs during a session. Do not add every finding feature to a small product, or insist every exploratory journey has one predetermined destination.

verification.question: What counts as enough information for this scenario? Can someone who lacks the exact term begin, someone with an exact target reach it, and a returning person recover a useful item where those needs are in scope?

principles.title: Support learning across search, browse and asking

source.heading: IA-03 — Support learning across search, browse and asking

triggers: A finding journey requires refinement, category exploration, related items, or a handoff to human help.
principles.exceptions: A direct factual lookup may need only a short path. A related-item recommendation must have a defensible relationship; neither a decorative carousel nor a speculative AI answer proves that relation. Asking is an architectural option, not permission to contact anyone or promise unavailable support.

verification.question: Starting from a useful result, can the person refine, broaden, discover related material and return with their context intact? Are the collection and query scope clear at each transition?

principles.title: Preserve semantic coherence while adapting channels and change rates

source.heading: IA-04 — Preserve semantic coherence while adapting channels and change rates

triggers: The same service spans native app, web, support or physical touchpoints, or a redesign changes the product's major sections.
principles.exceptions: Coherence does not require identical tabs, screen layouts or top-level ordering everywhere. Familiar patterns provide orientation but do not prohibit useful differentiation or expressive design. A metaphor may explain a domain while falsely implying capabilities; preserve its explanatory value without inheriting those false promises. Do not redesign all channels during a narrow requested edit.

verification.question: Can a person recognize the same object and its meaning across the relevant channels? Does each channel prioritize its own task without unexplained renaming? Can a plausible new content type fit without dissolving the existing categories?

principles.title: Design from both the overview and the individual content object

source.heading: IA-05 — Design from both the overview and the individual content object

triggers: Search, notifications, shared links or external links can bring people directly into a detail screen or document.
principles.exceptions: Not every detail requires global chrome or every metadata field on screen. Local context can be sufficient; exposing internal implementation is not the objective. A polished homepage cannot compensate for contextless deep entries, but a rich content model does not eliminate a useful overview either.

verification.question: On direct entry, can someone identify this item's type, context and available onward paths? Do proposed filters and related links have populated fields or relationships behind them? Is missing support recorded as a dependency?

principles.title: Choose organization schemes for the way people seek information

source.heading: IA-06 — Choose organization schemes for the way people seek information

triggers: Choosing category boundaries, sorting, browsing options, or how to combine unlike content types.
principles.exceptions: An alphabetic list is not necessarily useful to someone who lacks the target name; a topical tree is not automatically better for exact lookup. Geographic boundaries and naming can be contested. Multiple routes add maintenance and should answer real needs, not every conceivable perspective. Internal political compromises are constraints to disclose, not evidence that a grouping serves users.

verification.question: Can a content owner classify representative and ambiguous items consistently? Can intended users predict where those items belong, including items at different levels of granularity? Is the scheme explained independently of its menu presentation?

principles.title: Keep hybrid and audience routes understandable

source.heading: IA-07 — Keep hybrid and audience routes understandable

triggers: A menu mixes tasks, topics, audiences, formats or metaphors, or asks people to choose a role before seeing content.
principles.exceptions: Do not reject a useful global task link merely to achieve taxonomic purity. Role-specific experiences can be appropriate for genuine permissions or subscription differences. The issue is whether the structure remains predictable for actual tasks and overlapping roles, not whether every navigation label has the same grammatical form.

verification.question: Can someone explain the grouping rule without reading every option? Can a student who is also doing research reach relevant resources without creating a new identity or assuming they are excluded? Is an access restriction backed by actual product policy?

principles.title: Combine structures without rigid menu-count or depth rules

source.heading: IA-08 — Combine structures without rigid menu-count or depth rules

triggers: Designing a large hierarchy, a structured catalog, cross-listing, facets, related links or user tagging.
principles.exceptions: Hierarchy is a starting option, not a mandate for every product. Free tags can reveal user language and support social discovery but do not automatically supply consistent classification. The source's later warning about more than two or three levels is a dated heuristic, not a click-count acceptance test; a longer understandable route can outperform a short ambiguous one. Market outcomes of named tagging services are not proof of a general causal claim.

verification.question: Can users understand the current scope and move to useful alternatives without losing their bearings? Are cross-listings intentional, metadata fields populated, and tag-based recommendations distinguishable from curated structure? Does each level make a meaningful decision easier?

principles.title: Design a labeling system and check destination promises

source.heading: IA-09 — Design a labeling system and check destination promises

triggers: Renaming navigation, defining a new category set, using icons alone, or finding inconsistent link and page names.
principles.exceptions: Contextual prose links can legitimately vary; navigation labels need stronger stability because people encounter them repeatedly. Familiar specialist terms may suit a specialist audience. Brand language is acceptable when it remains interpretable; decorative novelty is not evidence of clarity. A justified mixed task/topic global menu need not be rewritten solely for grammatical uniformity.

verification.question: Before activating an important link, what content or action would the intended audience predict? Does the destination fulfill that expectation? Do the same words represent the same concept and different words distinguish different concepts across relevant states and channels?

principles.title: Treat candidate labels as hypotheses and maintain the vocabulary

source.heading: IA-10 — Treat candidate labels as hypotheses and maintain the vocabulary

triggers: Choosing terminology without direct evidence, reconciling novice and specialist language, or expanding a taxonomy.
principles.exceptions: Competitor prevalence, an author's suggestion and an automated extraction are candidate sources, not proof of comprehension. Search logs reveal expressed queries but not the complete need or success. Do not claim participants or research that did not occur. Do not infer statistical sufficiency from the source's example counts, create hypothetical product areas merely to fill every gap, or normalize away meaningful audience differences.

verification.question: What evidence supports this label, and what remains a hypothesis? Does it work in the real task as well as a card sort? Can plausible new content be classified without an unexplained 'Miscellaneous' bucket, and is there an owner for future changes?

principles.title: Orient people who enter anywhere

source.heading: IA-11 — Orient people who enter anywhere

triggers: Navigation, deep links, external search entry, notifications, or a content-heavy redesign.
principles.exceptions: These are semantic roles, not a mandate for three visible bars or desktop navigation on iPhone. A small app may satisfy several roles with one control. Do not force users through ancestors merely because the storage hierarchy has them. Conventional placement and icon examples from 2015 do not set current platform rules.

verification.question: From a direct link, can a person explain where they are, distinguish their next destinations, reach relevant related content, and return predictably? Is the orientation claim based on an actual traversal or only a static inspection?

principles.title: Offer complementary routes without making personalization the only map

source.heading: IA-12 — Offer complementary routes without making personalization the only map

triggers: A large collection, mixed user expertise, guided setup, or personalized discovery.
principles.exceptions: Do not require a sitemap, A–Z index, and tutorial in every product. Tiny environments may need none. Expert or repeated workflows can be burdened by guidance. Recommendations based on incomplete history can be wrong; social popularity can narrow discovery. A user-controlled favorite is different from an inferred recommendation.

verification.question: If a recommendation is irrelevant or a person does not share the assumed vocabulary, can they still reach the needed item? Can they exit a guide and revise a configuration without losing useful context?

principles.title: Decide whether search can be supported, not just whether it can be drawn

source.heading: IA-13 — Decide whether search can be supported, not just whether it can be drawn

triggers: Adding search, redesigning a search-heavy product, or proposing search to fix poor navigation.
principles.exceptions: Improving navigation is normally valuable, but search may be a practical interim route through fragmented content when structural repair is unavailable. Small, highly specific collections can still merit search. The book's suggested third-party products, algorithm counts, and historical expectations are not current selection guidance.

verification.question: For a representative query, can the team trace the intended item from source content through index and matching to an actionable result? Is a mock search distinguished from an implemented and exercised capability?

principles.title: Define the searchable unit and make scope legible

source.heading: IA-14 — Define the searchable unit and make scope legible

triggers: Mixed content types, fielded search, results polluted by navigation/boilerplate, or scoped search.
principles.exceptions: The book's navigation-versus-destination distinction is contextual, not a rule to exclude every category page. An overview can be the intended destination. Reviews and discussions may be valuable searchable content for some tasks despite the book's restaurant example. Do not hide useful items solely to obtain a smaller count.

verification.question: Can someone tell what was searched and intentionally change the scope? Do test queries retrieve the intended entity/field, including a relevant item outside the current zone after broadening?

principles.title: Match retrieval tradeoffs to the cost of misses and noise

source.heading: IA-15 — Match retrieval tradeoffs to the cost of misses and noise

triggers: Search ranking, query expansion, synonyms, spelling correction, or evaluation of retrieval quality.
principles.exceptions: Precision and recall often trade off under a particular change; they are not universally, mathematically inverse. Ch.9's absolute phrasing is stronger than Ch.10's own qualification. Do not claim corpus-level recall without knowing or estimating the relevant corpus. Existing engine behavior and evidence constrain promises; semantic or AI search still needs evaluation rather than an assumed guarantee.

verification.question: Which relevant items were missed, which irrelevant items were added, and why? Does a model/SKU/name query retain its intended specificity after normalization or expansion?

principles.title: Make results support recognition, judgment, and the next action

source.heading: IA-16 — Make results support recognition, judgment, and the next action

triggers: Search results, resource listings, comparisons, or result ranking/sorting controls.
principles.exceptions: More metadata can bury useful results; do not show all available fields. Popularity, expert recommendations, personal relevance, and paid placement are different signals. Do not imply payment proves quality or relevance, despite the book's favorable PFP speculation. Distinguish commercial promotion from ranking rationale. Historical “best bets” need real editorial ownership, not invented recommendations.

verification.question: Can a person distinguish similar results and explain the active order? Can they complete the intended next action without opening every result, while retaining essential consequences and provenance?

principles.title: Treat search as an iterative finding loop with recovery

source.heading: IA-17 — Treat search as an iterative finding loop with recovery

triggers: Search refinement, zero/many results, autocomplete, advanced search, or transitions between browse and search.
principles.exceptions: A single search field is a default, not a ban on well-labeled structured queries such as origin/destination. Advanced search can be the main workbench for expert tasks. Do not expose engine syntax merely to show technical detail. Autocomplete must not promise an unavailable result, and empty-state suggestions must not disguise an outage as “no matches.” Distinguishing transport/index failures is this skill's operational extension.

verification.question: With a misspelling, restrictive filter, empty result, and return from a detail view, can the person revise the search without reconstructing it? Do controls describe their actual scope and supported behavior?

principles.title: Accept users' vocabulary while maintaining stable concepts

source.heading: IA-18 — Accept users' vocabulary while maintaining stable concepts

triggers: Conflicting labels, synonyms, aliases, acronyms, localized names, misspellings, or content tagging.
principles.exceptions: Retrieval equivalence is context-dependent, not a claim that objects are interchangeable. The book groups competing devices and category names as equivalents in examples; do not silently replace a requested competitor/model with your own product. Related alternatives can be offered with explicit differences. A preferred term must not require users to know internal jargon.

verification.question: Do actual alternate terms reach the intended concept? Are broad or related matches visibly distinguishable from exact matches, and is a label change possible without breaking references?

principles.title: Choose vocabulary architecture according to what can actually be changed

source.heading: IA-19 — Choose vocabulary architecture according to what can actually be changed

triggers: Introducing a thesaurus, improving a legacy search system, or integrating external/dynamic content.
principles.exceptions: An indexing-only vocabulary does not automatically understand a user's variants. Query expansion without content tagging can increase noise and depends strongly on mapping quality. A vendor's claim of standards support does not establish compatible APIs, storage formats, or correct behavior. Check current standards only when implementing an actual compliance requirement.

verification.question: Where is vocabulary applied, what remains unsupported, and can a representative alias be traced through the implemented path? Is the maintenance workload realistic for the people and systems available?

principles.title: Model different semantic relationships explicitly

source.heading: IA-20 — Model different semantic relationships explicitly

triggers: Building a taxonomy, related-content network, terminology registry, or shared metadata model.
principles.exceptions: No universal noun-only, plural-only, or compound-term rule fits every context. Task navigation may need verbs; one collection may need a compound term that another can express with independent facets. Do not infer logical inheritance across every parent-child relationship or treat contextual association as equivalence.

verification.question: Can authors consistently classify a realistic ambiguous item? Are parent, alias, and related-item links distinguishable, reciprocal where intended, and useful for the specific finding task?

principles.title: Allow multiple routes to one item without multiplying the item

source.heading: IA-21 — Allow multiple routes to one item without multiplying the item

triggers: Content belongs in multiple categories, cross-listing, breadcrumbs, or inconsistent detail destinations.
principles.exceptions: Cross-listing every item everywhere creates noise and maintenance burden. Polyhierarchy is not equivalent to faceted filtering: the first permits multiple parents, while facets describe independent dimensions. The source says navigation context is the only real challenge; implementation also requires deduplication and maintenance discipline, which are operational extensions here.

verification.question: Do two category routes reach the same item and consistent facts? Can the person return to their original context without confusing that context with the object's only possible parent?

principles.title: Build facets from independent descriptive dimensions and usable metadata

source.heading: IA-22 — Build facets from independent descriptive dimensions and usable metadata

triggers: Filterable catalogs, document libraries, discovery, or a taxonomy mixing subject, audience, format, and location.
principles.exceptions: A filter panel cannot compensate for absent or unreliable metadata. Do not automatically expose every field or force the book's historical universal facets. Facet independence concerns principles of division, not a guarantee that values are statistically independent. Selection semantics and missing-value handling are this skill's build criteria rather than explicit book rules.

verification.question: Can representative items be described consistently, including one with missing metadata? Does a user reach the same result set through equivalent browse/search combinations, understand active constraints, and undo an overrestrictive combination?

principles.title: Plan research around the missing architectural evidence

source.heading: IA-23 — Plan research around the missing architectural evidence

triggers: Planning research for a major redesign with uncertain data, ownership, technical capacity, or user evidence.
principles.exceptions: Do not require interviews, kickoff meetings, all research methods, or a long report for every change. The source’s face-to-face imperative and meeting-size examples are historical working preferences. Existing authorization and access boundaries govern contact with stakeholders. Business goals constrain the design but do not justify inventing user needs.

verification.question: Does each consequential architectural choice fit the actual user task, content characteristics, and operational capacity? What would fail if an assumed capability or content owner did not exist?

principles.title: Study representative content before committing to categories or fields

source.heading: IA-24 — Study representative content before committing to categories or fields

triggers: Designing a catalog, library, knowledge base, search/filter system, or migration without a trustworthy understanding of its content.
principles.exceptions: A sample is not a complete migration inventory. Stop exploratory sampling when new examples cease to change the model, while stating its limits; use a complete accounting where the task requires migrating every item. Do not mechanically exclude rare content or impose the book’s suggested sample quantities. A pretty fixture set does not establish that production metadata supports facets.

verification.question: Can the proposed structure accommodate representative, unusually shaped, and important rare content? Which required fields are actually populated, and what will happen to objects that do not fit?

principles.title: Diagnose findability using search behavior and support evidence

source.heading: IA-25 — Diagnose findability using search behavior and support evidence

triggers: Users cannot find content, labels are disputed, queries return zero or excessive results, or analytics are being used to justify navigation changes.
principles.exceptions: Logs reflect the current product and observed population, not all potential needs. Popularity, dwell time, or departure alone do not establish usefulness, frustration, or causation. The source’s analytics product capabilities, tracking suggestions, and typical query-length examples are dated and are not an instruction to collect personal data or adopt surveillance. Missing logs stay an evidence gap.

verification.question: Can the proposed change explain and improve a specific findability failure? Is it repairing the actual cause, and have unchanged cases been considered?

principles.title: Choose an IA test for the uncertainty it can resolve

source.heading: IA-26 — Choose an IA test for the uncertainty it can resolve

triggers: Choosing category boundaries or labels, validating a new hierarchy, or claiming that a navigation structure is understandable.
principles.exceptions: A successful closed sort does not demonstrate successful navigation, and a successful stripped-down hierarchy test does not establish the finished UI’s usability. Qualitative cluster diagrams and small-sample percentages are not statistical proof. Focus groups can generate ideas but do not substitute for individual task performance. An agent inspection or synthetic sort is not a participant study; do not fabricate sessions or metrics. The source’s card counts, timing, and informal-friend examples are not universal research standards.

verification.question: Does the evidence method fit the claim? Can intended users find the destination under realistic wording, ambiguity, and entry conditions, or is that still a hypothesis?

principles.title: Turn research into a feasible architectural strategy

source.heading: IA-27 — Turn research into a feasible architectural strategy

triggers: Multiple plausible structures, substantial redesign, or research findings that have not become concrete implementation decisions.
principles.exceptions: Do not force a 50-page report, phase gate, or stakeholder presentation into a small task. The book’s 1999 Weather.com case illustrates a reasoning chain; its personalization, anonymous tracking, return-traffic objectives, and platform assumptions are not present-day recommendations. A screenshot or competitor example is not proof of a strategy’s outcomes.

verification.question: Can another contributor tell what changes, why, what supports the choice, and what must be built or maintained to make it real? Is a major unresolved assumption visible rather than hidden behind a diagram?

principles.title: Use different artifacts for structure, behavior, and semantics

source.heading: IA-28 — Use different artifacts for structure, behavior, and semantics

triggers: A sitemap is being treated as a complete specification, a wireframe is mistaken for final visual design, or a team cannot interpret a complex architecture diagram.
principles.exceptions: Do not generate every possible artifact or wireframe every repeated page. Text outlines or tables are acceptable when clearer. A wireframe is neither behavior validation nor the final visual direction; its typography and spacing are provisional unless deliberately specified. The book’s tool and printable-page conventions are dated. Its recommendation to present diagrams does not authorize contacting others.

verification.question: Can the intended implementer distinguish a container, content object, link, and state transition? Are consequential relationships and omissions clear, and do the views agree?

principles.title: Map content to destinations without confusing content with containers

source.heading: IA-29 — Map content to destinations without confusing content with containers

triggers: Content migration, splitting or combining pages, reusing information across channels, or translating a legacy structure into a new architecture.
principles.exceptions: Do not atomize every sentence or create a complex content system for a handful of static items. The book’s hierarchy-based IDs illustrate traceability, not a requirement to encode changeable hierarchy into permanent IDs. Preserve approved scope and dependencies; a mapping proposal does not authorize deleting or publishing content. Redirect and access-policy checks may be necessary implementation additions, but are not asserted as this passage’s explicit prescription.

verification.question: Can each required source item be traced to its intended destination or a documented disposition? Does updating reused content reach the correct places without creating contradictory copies?

principles.title: Make contextual navigation depend on explicit content relationships

source.heading: IA-30 — Make contextual navigation depend on explicit content relationships

triggers: Related content, product-to-review links, cross-sell, deep-linked detail pages, or a large collection that currently makes users restart at the hierarchy.
principles.exceptions: Manual curated links can suit small collections. Do not imply behavior-based recommendations exist without the necessary data or infer that “related” always means desirable. Popularity-based cross-sell is only one possible relationship. The book’s illustrative compound matching rule is not a guarantee of unique identity. Empty related sections or invented metadata must not conceal unavailable capability.

verification.question: For each visible relationship, can the system name its source, matching rule, and target? Does a duplicate-title case link to the right entity, and does missing data degrade honestly?

principles.title: Budget metadata and vocabularies as ongoing product capabilities

source.heading: IA-31 — Budget metadata and vocabularies as ongoing product capabilities

triggers: A proposal adds tags, facets, synonyms, cross-links, or fields without specifying how they will be populated and maintained.
principles.exceptions: The source’s sample maintenance ratings are contextual, not universal. Geographic, audience, and product vocabularies may be complex in another environment. Historical Word and LAN workflows are not implementation requirements. Shared/global fields and local/type-specific fields can coexist; centralized uniformity is not automatically best.

verification.question: Could the proposed filters and links be populated accurately now and maintained as content changes? Which field gives enough user value to justify its authoring and governance cost?

principles.title: Preserve the architectural rationale and maintain it through growth

source.heading: IA-32 — Preserve the architectural rationale and maintain it through growth

triggers: Content grows after launch, teams add new categories or terms, an organization changes, or a redesign risks discarding working structure.
principles.exceptions: No architecture is permanently correct, but growth is not automatic evidence for wholesale redesign. Do not invent ownership or schedule recurring monitoring without authorization. Documentation effort should fit the product; a small project may need only a few decision entries. Source examples such as mouseover-dependent guidance are historical, not current accessibility requirements.

verification.question: Could a new contributor add, rename, relate, index, or retire an object without silently breaking findability? Are approved rules, agent defaults, and unresolved assumptions distinguishable?

principles.title: Define the monitoring decision before choosing dashboard furniture

source.heading: DD-01 — Define the monitoring decision before choosing dashboard furniture

triggers: Designing a dashboard, KPI overview, status screen, or a request to make a product look like an executive dashboard.
principles.exceptions: The author's definition is an explicitly chosen useful boundary, not a reason to reject the user's product because it calls a scrollable analytics workspace a dashboard. Do not insist on graphics when concise text or a table communicates better. Historical vendor examples illustrate approaches rather than endorse products or establish current capabilities. Role-based customization means fitting the information need; it does not automatically require user-configurable widgets.

verification.question: Can each prominent item be connected to a stated monitoring objective and a useful next decision? Does the overview expose important conditions without pretending to contain every detail needed for diagnosis or action?

principles.title: Match cadence, detail, and interaction to the monitoring role

source.heading: DD-02 — Match cadence, detail, and interaction to the monitoring role

triggers: Choosing dashboard refresh behavior, alerting, detail level, historical context, or investigation controls.
principles.exceptions: The three roles are a useful lens, not exhaustive user types or mutually exclusive products. Do not inherit the source's dated assumptions that executives avoid computers or rarely analyze data. Strategic work can need interaction and analysts can investigate live data. Book examples of hover-to-detail do not justify hover-only access on touch or keyboard interfaces. Freshness/error-state checks are this skill's operational extension of the cadence argument.

verification.question: Does the refresh/detail contract fit the time available to make the decision? Can someone distinguish a current condition, a historical snapshot, and stale or unavailable data, and reach the appropriate investigation or response without losing scope?

principles.title: Keep decision-critical comparisons visible together

source.heading: DD-03 — Keep decision-critical comparisons visible together

triggers: Splitting a dashboard into tabs, a carousel, per-item views, nested scroll regions, or a dense mobile overview.
principles.exceptions: The book's strict single-screen definition reflects its monitoring focus. Do not shrink text, suppress necessary context, disable zoom, or violate native text-scaling/reflow behavior to satisfy a no-scroll rule. Scrolling and multiple views are legitimate for other purposes and accessibility configurations. Describe any loss of simultaneous comparison and compensate for it; this responsive/accessibility adaptation is the skill's judgment, not a claim that the 2006 book prescribed mobile behavior.

verification.question: Can the intended comparison be made from the currently visible content without remembering hidden values? At supported narrow widths and enlarged text, are decision groups still understandable and critical conditions reachable without clipped or illegible content?

principles.title: Give each metric enough context to support an interpretation

source.heading: DD-04 — Give each metric enough context to support an interpretation

triggers: KPI tiles, status indicators, targets, current-versus-prior comparisons, or an unlabeled gauge that looks informative.
principles.exceptions: More comparison data is not automatically better; omit references that do not change the decision. A target may be aspirational while a historical norm is descriptive. An annual target beside month-to-date performance is not inherently invalid, but must not imply a same-period performance comparison. Metric ownership, denominator validation, missing-state handling and data provenance are implementation checks extending the source's context principle. A screenshot cannot verify the underlying calculations or freshness.

verification.question: Can someone tell what this value measures, over which period and population, relative to what, and why its status was assigned? Do missing, partial, stale and incompatible comparisons remain visibly distinct from measured success or failure?

principles.title: Use a direct measure and precision appropriate to the decision

source.heading: DD-05 — Use a direct measure and precision appropriate to the decision

triggers: Metric calculation, denominator or percentage-change questions; a dashboard makes users calculate a variance, displays many decimals, or compresses operational values into abbreviated numbers.
principles.exceptions: A percentage can exaggerate a change from a tiny base or conceal a large absolute impact. Reduced precision is inappropriate where a threshold, reconciliation, safety judgment or financial commitment depends on the exact value. Do not infer significance or certainty from decimal places. Denominator edge cases and percentage-point distinctions are the skill's computational checks, not explicit formulas supplied by this passage.

verification.question: Can the intended judgment be made without avoidable arithmetic, and does the derived measure retain the context needed to avoid a misleading conclusion? Test boundary values, negative values, missing/zero denominators and rounding near thresholds when those states are possible.

principles.title: Choose an encoding for the question, not for visual variety

source.heading: DD-06 — Choose an encoding for the question, not for visual variety

triggers: Selecting charts for a dashboard, replacing tables with graphics, adding pies, bubbles, radar charts or maps, or trying to make repeated charts look less repetitive.
principles.exceptions: Few's blanket rejection of pie charts is the author's position; the skill should evaluate a requested chart by its task, valid data and comparison precision rather than impose an unsupported universal ban. Area or spatial encodings may serve other tasks, but do not treat them as equally precise for comparisons of close values. Preserve useful brand expression and approved choices while explaining an evidenced encoding problem. The source examples are expert critiques, not controlled comparative studies.

verification.question: Does the chart's implied relationship actually exist in the data? Can the intended comparison be made without decoding unrelated shapes, memorizing a legend, or mistaking area for diameter? Is repeated visual treatment stable enough to reuse a reading strategy?

principles.title: Keep quantitative geometry truthful and important values visible

source.heading: DD-07 — Keep quantitative geometry truthful and important values visible

triggers: Bar chart baseline or truncated scales, decorative perspective, occluded marks, inconsistent axes, or a chart whose labels and marks imply different values.
principles.exceptions: Zero-baseline guidance for magnitude bars does not imply every line or point chart must start at zero, or that interval/range marks encode magnitude from zero. Data with negative values needs an honest zero reference and signed extent. Purposeful 3-D spatial work is outside the source's typical business-chart case. Current accessibility and interaction requirements govern how equivalent information is exposed.

verification.question: Does the visible mark encode the value it claims, with the intended baseline, units and domain? Can a viewer inspect every consequential value without hidden marks or perspective errors, and are visual comparisons valid across neighboring plots?

principles.title: Reserve emphasis for meaningful differences and consequential conditions

source.heading: DD-08 — Reserve emphasis for meaningful differences and consequential conditions

triggers: Dashboards with competing card headers, multiple bright palettes, prominent chrome, arbitrary chart colors, or related measures placed far apart.
principles.exceptions: Do not turn the author's strong aesthetic opinions into a ban on personality, logos, gradients or all decoration throughout the product. A simulation may legitimately resemble equipment. A fixed top-left priority rule depends on reading direction, layout and use; the task's actual attention needs govern placement. Color-vision prevalence figures and claims that decoration inevitably becomes annoying are dated source assertions, not fresh evidence. Exact contrast, assistive output and motion behavior require applicable current standards and runtime checks.

verification.question: In the relevant task state, does the most consequential condition stand out for a reason, and can it be understood without relying only on color? Do grouping and repeated visual codes support the intended comparison rather than imply false relationships?

principles.title: Choose visual attributes for the kind of comparison

source.heading: DD-09 — Choose visual attributes for the kind of comparison

triggers: Selecting marks, colors, sizes or positions to encode a measure or distinguish categories.
principles.exceptions: The book's suggested small counts of discriminable attributes are heuristics, not universal palette, menu or chart limits. Area can be useful for overview and hierarchy despite its weaker precision. Do not infer that all intensity encodings work for every viewer, that hue has an inherent numeric order, or that a fast visual pop-out guarantees comprehension. Motion advice in the book does not justify flashing alerts; use current accessibility and platform requirements.

verification.question: Can someone answer the intended comparison without estimating an unreliable area ratio or memorizing a legend? Are category identity, numerical amount and significance encoded distinctly? Does the encoding remain understandable without color alone?

principles.title: Group by relationships and reduce comparison memory

source.heading: DD-10 — Group by relationships and reduce comparison memory

triggers: Arranging dashboard panels, tables, related measures or a process diagram.
principles.exceptions: Do not convert the author's memory figures into an arbitrary item limit, or his simultaneous-view preference into a prohibition on scrolling, zoom, accessible reflow or detail views. Preserve the comparison through pinned context, a summary or a dedicated comparison view when one screen cannot reasonably contain it. Similar-looking metrics must not imply shared units or interchangeable meaning when they differ.

verification.question: What must the person remember while moving between these items? Does whitespace imply the intended groups? Could a border, shared color or connecting line suggest a false relationship?

principles.title: Separate enduring priority from temporary exceptions

source.heading: DD-11 — Separate enduring priority from temporary exceptions

triggers: Establishing dashboard hierarchy, alert states or updates to a frequently revisited monitoring view.
principles.exceptions: Do not rearrange the whole dashboard on every refresh just to promote the latest alert. Intentionally ranked exception queues can reorder when their ordering is visible and interaction remains stable. The book's preferred reading positions depend on reading direction and task. Its intensity-only accessibility claims and suggestion of at most two alert levels are not guarantees or quotas. Required controls, active filters and critical values must remain discoverable and sufficiently contrasted.

verification.question: Can a returning user find the same measure? Can they explain the highlighted condition and its severity without color? Is the most vivid element actually the one requiring attention?

principles.title: Remove visual interference while preserving useful scaffolding

source.heading: DD-12 — Remove visual interference while preserving useful scaffolding

triggers: Simplifying an overloaded table, graph or dashboard, or applying a minimalist visual direction.
principles.exceptions: Data versus nondata is not the same as useful versus useless. Do not erase zero lines, scope, units, uncertainty, thresholds, source freshness or control affordances to make the screen look quieter. The book's advice to mute controls or put them toward the bottom right is contextual, not a rule for filters and actions essential to the task.
