Light styling must still satisfy current accessibility requirements at actual size.

verification.question: Which specific task does each remaining line, label, background and control support? After simplification, can users still locate the scope, follow a row, estimate values and distinguish groups? Did visual quiet make an essential state invisible?

principles.title: Summarize for the decision without hiding the underlying situation

source.heading: DD-13 — Summarize for the decision without hiding the underlying situation

triggers: Choosing dashboard detail, aggregation, historical windows or an exception-only presentation.
principles.exceptions: Executive overview and transaction reconciliation demand different precision. Rounding should match the decision and retain exact values when required. An apparently stable aggregate can hide subgroups, tails or missing observations; add distribution or segmentation when those change the action. Additional periods are not useful merely because data exists. The book's preference for summary does not authorize discarding detail needed for diagnosis or audit.

verification.question: What could this summary conceal that would reverse the decision? Is the state still interpretable when no alerts exist? Are windows, aggregation and partial-period comparisons apparent without opening several unrelated screens?

principles.title: Select text or graphics by the question, not the dashboard label

source.heading: DD-14 — Select text or graphics by the question, not the dashboard label

triggers: Choosing among a number, table, chart, map or treemap for a dashboard item.
principles.exceptions: Tables may legitimately contain sparklines or bullet graphs. A graph is not mandatory on every card. Treemap prominence identifies a candidate for investigation, not automatically the greatest business loss: revenue area plus percent-of-quota color alone does not establish every measure of impact. Use bars or a table for accurate ranking. The author's criticisms of pies, radar and area graphs explain comparison weaknesses; they should not become unqualified bans divorced from task or natural data structure.

verification.question: State the exact question this representation answers. Can users retrieve an exact value if necessary? Does geographic placement or nested area add information the decision actually uses? Could a simpler representation make the intended comparison more reliable?

principles.title: Make compact performance comparisons honest

source.heading: DD-15 — Make compact performance comparisons honest

triggers: Bullet graph or gauge selection; displaying actual performance against a target, acceptable range or forecast.
principles.exceptions: Threshold bands need a defensible source; do not invent bad/acceptable/good ranges to fill a component. Lower values may be better, and target crossing can be harmful. The book's preferred number of bands is not a universal limit. Bullet graphs are a useful option, not a required replacement for every gauge or number. Few explicitly describes his comparison experiments as too small to support scientific performance claims.

verification.question: Is the bar baseline honest? Can the user distinguish actual, target, acceptable range and projection? Are target period, direction of improvement and units clear? Would removing unsupported bands make the display more truthful?

principles.title: Let the relationship determine bars, lines and composition

source.heading: DD-16 — Let the relationship determine bars, lines and composition

triggers: Comparing categories, changes over time, parts of a total or two related measures.
principles.exceptions: Chart types are means, not absolute rules: a cumulative relationship justifies connected categories, and coarse composition may justify stacking. The book recommends dual-axis combinations in some examples, but independently chosen scales can imply arbitrary relationships. Prefer a shared unit/scale or aligned separate panels when possible; if dual axes are essential, label the mapping and avoid interpreting crossings or slopes as evidence of a relationship. Avoid silently joining gaps or irregular observations as if equally spaced measurements existed.

verification.question: What does each connection mean? Which segments have a common baseline? Could the same data look strongly related merely by changing one axis? Are scale, ordering, intervals and denominator visible?

principles.title: Give miniature history enough context to mean something

source.heading: DD-17 — Give miniature history enough context to mean something

triggers: Adding a sparkline, trend arrow or compact historical display beside a current value.
principles.exceptions: An axis-free sparkline can be appropriate for a within-series shape question, but it does not establish exact magnitude or cross-series amplitude by itself. The author's claim that a sparkline removes ambiguity needs this qualification: an unlabeled window or independently rescaled series can still mislead. An arrow can work when its comparison and meaning are explicit; it is not intrinsically bad.

verification.question: Over what period is this trend? Does the current label match the final mark? Are two apparently similar slopes actually comparable? Can someone distinguish zero, missing observations and a not-yet-complete period?

principles.title: Show variation when a center value conceals the decision

source.heading: DD-18 — Show variation when a center value conceals the decision

triggers: Monitoring compensation, latency, defects, delivery times or any measure where tails, spread or subgroups matter.
principles.exceptions: The book's statement that a median is the center of the range is imprecise: it is the ordered middle (the 50th percentile), not necessarily the midpoint of minimum and maximum. Its illustrated percentile whiskers are one convention, not the universal box-plot definition. Simplifying a plot for overview must not erase the tails the task is meant to detect; a small sample may be clearer as individual observations.

verification.question: Could two populations with the displayed summary require different actions? What exactly do whiskers and dots mean here? Are absent observations, sample size or changed population definitions affecting the comparison?

principles.title: Show associations without implying causation or confusing slope with strength

source.heading: DD-19 — Show associations without implying causation or confusing slope with strength

triggers: Investigating relationships between paired numerical measures or comparing relationships across groups.
principles.exceptions: Association is not evidence of causation. A steeper fitted line measures a different change per unit; it does not by itself indicate stronger correlation. Do not repeat the source's description of the steeper example as a more positive correlation. The book's preference for straight fits is not a reason to hide a nonlinear pattern. Axis changes can alter apparent slope, and aggregation or shared time trends can complicate interpretation.

verification.question: Are the observations paired correctly? Does the fit describe the points rather than impose a story? Would labels, subgroups, changed units or axis limits alter the claimed interpretation? Is a causal conclusion unsupported by this display?

principles.title: Use small multiples as a controlled comparison

source.heading: DD-20 — Use small multiples as a controlled comparison

triggers: Comparing the same measures across regions, channels, cohorts or periods without overloading one plot.
principles.exceptions: A repeated chart is not comparable merely because it looks consistent. Different time windows, denominators or populations can invalidate the intended comparison. Remove duplicated labels only when readers can still associate them reliably; responsive stacking may require repeating them. The author's expectation of future vendor support is historical, not an implementation constraint, and his example does not prove that one chart can never represent another dimension.

verification.question: What stays constant across panels, and what changes? Can users compare the intended values without mentally translating scales or relocating missing labels? Does the layout preserve these conditions after reflow?

principles.title: Arrange the overview around the relationships people need to use

source.heading: DD-21 — Arrange the overview around the relationships people need to use

triggers: A monitoring screen contains many metrics, operational areas, business entities or related charts.
principles.exceptions: The organization chart is not automatically the user's mental model. Whitespace is a means of grouping, not a target to maximize: the sales critique on PDF154 points out that excessive blank space can leave tables needlessly small. The upper-left emphasis in the book's desktop examples is not a universal reading-order rule across writing systems, native layouts and assistive navigation.

verification.question: Can the intended user follow the relevant overview-to-exception sequence without searching distant panels for the comparator or context? Does the grouping survive the actual viewport and text-size conditions?

principles.title: Make the comparison meaningful before making it visually easy

source.heading: DD-22 — Make the comparison meaningful before making it visually easy

triggers: Comparing measures across panels, normalizing to targets, combining different units, or placing trends side by side.
principles.exceptions: Do not adopt the book's dual-axis example as a default: two arbitrary scale choices can create a false impression of agreement or relationship. Prefer aligned separate plots or a clearly explained normalization when they answer the task more honestly; justify a dual axis if retained. A time-normalized trend and a magnitude comparison are different tasks, and a universal shared numeric scale can hide useful variation. These scale and comparison-contract checks extend the source's contextual reasoning; static graphs cannot establish correlation or cause.

verification.question: Could someone infer an incorrect relationship because scales, denominators, periods or definitions differ? Can they distinguish relative attainment from actual amount and an observed result from an expectation?

principles.title: Keep visual meaning consistent across the whole dashboard

source.heading: DD-23 — Keep visual meaning consistent across the whole dashboard

triggers: Multiple teams or chart components contribute colors, status treatments, axes, legends or interaction styles to one dashboard.
principles.exceptions: Consistency does not mean every measure must use the same graph or every page the same composition. Different questions may require different encodings. A scoped legend can explain legitimate local differences, but repeatedly changing the meaning of a prominent status color still imposes a cost. The author's beliefs that certain historical hues remain distinguishable to color-blind viewers are not accessibility verification.

verification.question: If the same visual cue appears in two sections, does it communicate the same meaning or clearly establish a different scope? Can key states be identified without depending on hue alone?

principles.title: Apply visual restraint without sacrificing legibility or useful character

source.heading: DD-24 — Apply visual restraint without sacrificing legibility or useful character

triggers: Dense metrics become visually exhausting, tables are too small, ornament competes with data, or a redesign strips away all personality in the name of simplicity.
principles.exceptions: The book's preferred off-white canvas, muted nature colors and restricted font palette are contextual design preferences, not universal requirements or a ban on dark mode. A photo or illustration can be task information, not mere decoration. Do not lower contrast until boundaries or marks disappear, or shrink text to satisfy the one-screen ideal. Current platform/accessibility requirements and the project's accepted visual direction govern implementation.

verification.question: Does the visual emphasis lead to decision-relevant information, and is that information comfortably readable under actual display conditions? Which removed or retained element has a concrete role?

principles.title: Connect the overview to details through a coherent interaction contract

source.heading: DD-25 — Connect the overview to details through a coherent interaction contract

triggers: Dashboard drill-down, filters or detail navigation after an exception; the overview needs to lead into investigation or action.
principles.exceptions: Do not make tiny graphical marks or hover the sole way to obtain necessary values or actions. Explicit controls can be clearer and more accessible than the source's preference for eliminating separate buttons. An overview can legitimately be static when the job does not require interaction. State preservation, accessibility and capability checks are this skill's extensions; a static source image does not show them working.

verification.question: Starting from a consequential signal, can a person identify and activate the next step, retain the relevant scope, and return to the same investigation context on the intended platform?

principles.title: Validate interpretation with realistic tasks and state the coaching boundary

source.heading: DD-26 — Validate interpretation with realistic tasks and state the coaching boundary

triggers: A dashboard introduces unfamiliar encodings, a team claims it is intuitive, or a polished prototype is being treated as evidence of user comprehension.
principles.exceptions: Do not make one-prototype-only a rule, block requested alternatives, or treat a user's disagreement as ignorance. Matched alternatives can test a real uncertainty. Do not assume only minor changes will be needed or coach someone and then claim first-use discoverability. Neither an agent walkthrough nor agreement with the author's examples is a participant study; no recruitment or external contact is authorized by this source.

verification.question: What did actual participants correctly detect and interpret, under what task and instruction conditions? If no such study occurred, is the report explicit about what remains untested?

principles.title: Separate live, stale, paused, acknowledged and resolved states

source.heading: DD-27 — Separate live, stale, paused, acknowledged and resolved states

triggers: Operational monitoring, frequent refreshes, temporary display freezing, alerts, or a dashboard mixing strategic and near-real-time information.
principles.exceptions: Do not automatically adopt blinking, escalating sound, or auto-reset behavior from the 2006 examples. Critical monitoring may require alerts to remain active while the visual snapshot is paused; confirm the domain's contract instead of inventing it. The source's statement that no red circles means nothing is wrong assumes functioning current input. Timestamps, stale-data states and distinct acknowledgment/resolution semantics are implementation safeguards derived from the example, not explicit book specifications.

verification.question: Can someone tell whether the value is current, stale or intentionally frozen, and whether an alert was silenced or actually resolved? Have update failure, pause/resume and new-alert behavior been exercised rather than merely drawn?

principles.title: Audit decision coverage before judging the dashboard's polish

source.heading: DD-28 — Audit decision coverage before judging the dashboard's polish

triggers: Reviewing a complete dashboard, comparing design alternatives, or accepting a concise display that may hide important context.
principles.exceptions: The book explicitly says its example metric lists are illustrative, not universal sales/CIO/telesales requirements. Do not add pipeline, top-ten lists, employee rankings or behavioral tracking merely because they appear in an example. A dashboard with eight varied widgets is not inherently complete, and a table-only solution is not inherently wrong. The source's critiques predict costs; they do not establish measured performance gains. On small or enlarged-text screens, preserve coherent comparisons through adaptive grouping/detail rather than prohibiting scrolling or making data unreadable.

verification.question: Which important question can no longer be answered after simplification or styling? Can the viewer determine both the signal and its consequence without an undocumented encoding or unavailable comparison?

principles.title: Jakob: transfer expectations before copying appearance

source.heading: LU-01 — Jakob: transfer expectations before copying appearance

triggers: Jakob law mental models familiar conventions pattern innovation sameness
principles.exceptions: An established convention may be harmful or inappropriate to this domain. A new interaction is reasonable when its task benefit outweighs relearning and can be demonstrated with users. Do not infer a universal mental model from a popular app or invent research-backed personas.

verification.question: Can intended users predict what this familiar or deliberately new interaction will do?

principles.title: Jakob: design the transition when learned workflows change

source.heading: LU-02 — Jakob: design the transition when learned workflows change

triggers: Jakob redesign migration transition returning users changed workflow relearning
principles.exceptions: Maintaining two experiences has real cost and may be impossible for a safety fix or incompatible data model. Preview and reversion are options, not mandatory release gates. Historical business outcomes in the chapter do not prove a single design change caused them.

verification.question: Can returning users complete the old task in the new structure, and does the stated transition or fallback actually preserve the promised state?

principles.title: Fitts: evaluate acquisition paths and effective targets

source.heading: LU-03 — Fitts: evaluate acquisition paths and effective targets

triggers: Fitts law target size distance pointing acquisition label activation screen edge
principles.exceptions: The historical pointing model is not an end-to-end usability formula. A screenshot cannot establish the hit region. Desktop cursor-edge benefits depend on actual pointer boundaries and do not transfer automatically to touch, multi-display layouts, or embedded windows. Do not enlarge or move a control at the expense of meaning, safety, or readable content.

verification.question: Can supported inputs activate the intended effective target along the real task path without a competing action firing?

principles.title: Fitts: investigate conditions behind target errors

source.heading: LU-04 — Fitts: investigate conditions behind target errors

triggers: Fitts human factors grip reach adjacent targets contextual inquiry misselection
principles.exceptions: One center-accuracy illustration, one grip, or an author anecdote cannot certify comfort or predict this product’s error rate. The chapter’s minimum-size table combines distinct units and contexts; do not copy its WCAG row as a universal requirement. Follow the adopted current standard and platform guidance, then test actual conditions. Never stage distracting field research in unsafe conditions.

verification.question: Were near misses, opposing actions, and relevant physical conditions examined with evidence appropriate to the claim?

principles.title: Miller: make chunks meaningful to the task

source.heading: LU-05 — Miller: make chunks meaningful to the task

triggers: Miller law chunking meaningful groups hierarchy dense content memory
principles.exceptions: A decorative card is not automatically a meaningful chunk. Expertise, content familiarity, language and task affect what forms a useful unit. Do not force every group to the same size or substitute a numeric quota for information architecture.

verification.question: Do the groups express task-relevant relationships and preserve the information needed for comparison?

principles.title: Miller: distinguish visible choice from memory demand

source.heading: LU-06 — Miller: distinguish visible choice from memory demand

triggers: Miller seven plus minus two 7±2 menu item limit working memory visible navigation
principles.exceptions: Do not replace seven with four or another universal quota. A large visible menu can still fail through poor information scent, crowded targets or excess search effort; visibility alone does not guarantee usability. Reducing choices requires a task-specific reason.

verification.question: Does the design address an identified memory or findability demand instead of enforcing a fixed visible-item quota?

principles.title: Hick: reduce decision effort for the actual choice

source.heading: LU-07 — Hick: reduce decision effort for the actual choice

triggers: Hick Hyman law choices decision time progressive disclosure choice overload card sorting
principles.exceptions: The historical stimulus-response formula does not predict an arbitrary purchase, search or expert workflow. More steps can add navigation and memory costs; fewer visible choices can conceal the right answer. The book’s jam-study and streaming examples are accounts, not a universal conversion guarantee. Do not invent measured time savings.

verification.question: Does the choice structure support the actual decision and preserve useful alternatives, context and correction?

principles.title: Hick: keep the cues that make simplicity understandable

source.heading: LU-08 — Hick: keep the cues that make simplicity understandable

triggers: Hick oversimplification icon labels abstraction hidden controls contextual cues
principles.exceptions: More text is not always better: familiar compact controls may work when meaning and accessibility remain clear. Do not prescribe labels for every decorative mark or preserve redundant explanation indefinitely. The chapter’s adjacent app screenshots are examples, not a controlled labeled/unlabeled experiment.

verification.question: Are enough cues retained to understand the action and finish the full task without guessing?

principles.title: Apply Postel’s law through explicit input boundaries

source.heading: LU-09 — Apply Postel’s law through explicit input boundaries

triggers: Postel robustness principle input tolerance names addresses normalization ambiguous dates
safe parsing cultural input assumptions interviews
principles.exceptions: Tolerance is not permission to guess identity, dates, destinations or amounts, weaken required validation, or accept malformed data at a security boundary. Author’s network analogy is not a parser-security prescription. Avoid redundant research for an approved routine correction.

verification.question: Can representative valid variants be entered and recovered after error, while ambiguous input receives a clear resolution path rather than a silent guess?

principles.title: Preserve a usable baseline when capabilities or content change

source.heading: LU-10 — Preserve a usable baseline when capabilities or content change

triggers: progressive enhancement capability denied failed unavailable voice fallback
text expansion font scaling writing direction resilient layout
principles.exceptions: A feature can legitimately require a capability; explain that dependency and a viable alternative where one exists. The book’s Amazon example removes lower-priority links as text grows; this does not justify losing essential actions. Its text-expansion ratio is an illustration, not a universal layout multiplier. Do not claim a baseline works for everyone without evidence.

verification.question: With the optional capability absent and content expanded, can the intended user still find, complete and recover the essential task?

principles.title: Use the peak–end rule to locate evidenced journey risks

source.heading: LU-11 — Use the peak–end rule to locate evidenced journey risks

triggers: peak end rule journey emotional moments retrospective remembered experience
journey mapping emotional curve evidence hypothesis owner outcome
principles.exceptions: The laboratory and medical studies summarized in the book do not prove a fixed averaging formula for every digital journey. A beautiful ending cannot establish that earlier difficulty was harmless, and an invented persona or emotional curve is not participant evidence. Use a compact annotation when a full map adds no decision value.

verification.question: Which evidenced or explicitly hypothesized moment is being improved, what outcome should change, and how will that be distinguished from a favorable retrospective rating?

principles.title: Repair negative peaks and make endings truthful

source.heading: LU-12 — Repair negative peaks and make endings truthful

triggers: negative peak truthful ending completion confirmation pending celebration humor
peak end failure recovery wait status password constraints
principles.exceptions: Do not deliberately prolong work, manufacture an emotional peak, conceal service failure or celebrate an unconfirmed outcome to improve recall. The password example illustrates visible constraint feedback, not an endorsement of its historical password policy. Humor and gamification are optional expressive choices, not remedies for loss or distress.

verification.question: Can the person tell success from pending or failed work, recover without unnecessary repetition, and finish with the needed outcome and next step clearly available?

principles.title: Treat aesthetic–usability as a perception effect to investigate

source.heading: LU-13 — Treat aesthetic–usability as a perception effect to investigate

triggers: aesthetic usability effect apparent ease inherent usability visual appeal trust
beautiful polished interface perceived usability task success
principles.exceptions: Do not conclude that attractive products are objectively safe or usable, that disliked styling causes every task failure, or that all interfaces should imitate the book’s Braun/Apple examples. The reported rapid first-impression timing is not a current acceptance threshold, and correlation of ratings is not proof that ornament improves completion.

verification.question: Which claim is supported by appeal ratings, which by observed behavior, and which remains a hypothesis after the comparison?

principles.title: Look past praise when testing a polished interface

source.heading: LU-14 — Look past praise when testing a polished interface

triggers: aesthetic masking usability testing praise satisfaction observed task failure
neutral prompts synthesis observations interpretation participant evidence
principles.exceptions: Neither praise nor a single hesitation should be discarded to fit a theory. Think-aloud, observation and task wording can influence behavior; record these conditions. Agent inspection and scripted checks cannot become participant findings, and testing does not authorize recruitment or external contact without the user’s request.

verification.question: Does the report retain material task failures even when satisfaction is high, and connect each proposed fix to observed evidence or an explicitly labeled inference?

principles.title: Use von Restorff distinctiveness in service of the user’s decision

source.heading: LU-15 — Use von Restorff distinctiveness in service of the user’s decision

triggers: von Restorff isolation effect selective attention banner blindness change blindness
salience destructive button pricing plan notification emphasis
principles.exceptions: A memorable or clicked element is not necessarily understood, appropriate or beneficial. Do not hide cheaper plans, manufacture popularity or urgency, or turn destructive action into the visually preferred choice merely because it is important. The book’s red Delete example illustrates differentiation; it is not evidence that that treatment prevents accidental deletion in the current flow.

verification.question: Can the person identify the relevant action and its consequences while still seeing legitimate alternatives, and does the emphasis clarify a user need rather than bias an uninformed choice?

principles.title: Verify attention cues without equating gaze with understanding

source.heading: LU-16 — Verify attention cues without equating gaze with understanding

triggers: von Restorff attention contrast noncolor cues reduced motion
eye tracking fixation heatmap gaze comprehension emotional inference
principles.exceptions: A fixation, heatmap or glance does not by itself establish understanding, preference, emotion, consent or task success. An agent’s visual scan is not eye tracking. Do not require expensive gaze research when a simpler observation answers the question, or remove all useful emphasis in the name of restraint.

verification.question: Does the cue retain its meaning under the relevant accessibility conditions, and are claims about attention, comprehension and emotion limited to the evidence actually collected?

principles.title: Tesler’s law: assign complexity without hiding consequential choices

source.heading: LU-17 — Tesler’s law: assign complexity without hiding consequential choices

triggers: Tesler law conservation complexity repeated entry automation natural language inferred values
principles.exceptions: Conservation is a design heuristic, not a measured quantity or proof that complexity cannot be eliminated by changing the process. Automation can add verification and recovery work. Historical AI/retail examples do not establish present capability or reliability; do not assume a natural-language interface makes expertise unnecessary.

verification.question: Can a person see and correct a wrong reused or inferred value before commitment, and does the complete task require less work including recovery?

principles.title: Preserve discoverability when disclosing complexity progressively

source.heading: LU-18 — Preserve discoverability when disclosing complexity progressively

triggers: Tesler progressive disclosure active user hidden advanced settings contextual guidance
principles.exceptions: People sometimes do read documentation; the author’s absolute wording is not a universal trait. Hiding choices can move effort into search or recall. The illustrated hover menu is a historical example, not a complete keyboard, touch or assistive-technology specification.

verification.question: Without a prior tutorial, can the intended person find the needed advanced control and understand its consequence, including from an alternate entry and supported input method?

principles.title: Doherty threshold: measure response stages in the actual task

source.heading: LU-19 — Doherty threshold: measure response stages in the actual task

triggers: Doherty threshold 400ms 400 ms response time latency skeleton loading useful content durable completion
principles.exceptions: The book’s400ms,100ms and10-second examples are contextual historical guidance, not universal acceptance thresholds or proof of productivity gains. A fast acknowledgment does not establish completed work. Skeletons can mislead if they imply unavailable content, and animation must respect applicable motion/accessibility needs.

verification.question: Under representative slow conditions, when is input acknowledged, useful work available and the outcome committed; does feedback preserve context without misrepresenting completion?

principles.title: Keep perceived progress and optimistic updates truthful

source.heading: LU-20 — Keep perceived progress and optimistic updates truthful

triggers: Doherty perceived performance fake progress artificial delay optimistic UI rollback pending confirmed
principles.exceptions: This adaptation deliberately limits the book’s favorable statements about inaccurate progress and artificial delay. Do not fabricate work, completion or precision to manufacture trust. Optimism is unsuitable where a false success indication could cause serious loss or irreversible action; a persistent confirmation can make a fast result understandable without delaying it.

verification.question: Do slow, failed, canceled and retried requests show the actual state, with a workable correction path and no fabricated progress or hidden extra commitment?

principles.title: Turn psychological explanations into revisable product decisions

source.heading: LU-21 — Turn psychological explanations into revisable product decisions

triggers: psychological laws design principles three choices80 characters goal observation rule heuristic evidence
principles.exceptions: A named law is not evidence that this design will work for this audience, and matching a law does not validate a team’s chosen limit. The illustrative numbers are not source-derived standards. Routine approved changes do not require a principles workshop or a new document.

verification.question: Can the team name a real decision the principle changes, its scope and tradeoff, and the observation that would make it revise the rule?

principles.title: Build shared design judgment through concrete cases and feedback

source.heading: LU-22 — Build shared design judgment through concrete cases and feedback

triggers: design principles team alignment gatekeeper shared judgment workshop dot voting
principles.exceptions: Workshop agreement and dot voting express team preference, not participant evidence or scientific validation. Do not let consistency preserve a harmful pattern, replace research or create an approval gate for every reversible change. Adopt only as much process as recurring coordination problems justify.

verification.question: Can two reviewers use the guidance to explain the same consequential tradeoff, while still recording disagreement and evidence that warrants an exception?

principles.title: Judge engagement mechanisms against the person’s goal and control

source.heading: LU-23 — Judge engagement mechanisms against the person’s goal and control

triggers: ethical design engagement autonomy dark patterns defaults autoplay infinite scroll personalization variable rewards
principles.exceptions: Do not infer addiction, neurological effects or intent from a screenshot, nor treat old platform examples or reported usage counts as present facts. The presence of a reward or feed alone does not establish harm; examine its actual function, context, and user evidence. Increased time spent is not automatically success.

verification.question: Can a person understand and decline the nudge, finish and leave, change the default, or stop the loop without losing unrelated functionality?

principles.title: Test consequential nonideal scenarios and retain useful friction

source.heading: LU-24 — Test consequential nonideal scenarios and retain useful friction

triggers: ethical design nonideal scenarios unintended consequences useful friction deliberation qualitative metrics
principles.exceptions: This is targeted review, not a demand for every conceivable edge case or an automatic approval step. Extra friction can itself exclude people or obstruct cancellation. The book’s broad mental-health claims are not a basis for diagnosing users or asserting causal effects in this product; actual research is required for such claims.

verification.question: For each relevant consequential scenario, does the design preserve understanding and a feasible escape or correction path, and is retained friction proportionate to the consequence?

principles.title: Resolve a useful feature slice before speculative shell styling

source.heading: RU-01 — Resolve a useful feature slice before speculative shell styling

triggers: A new feature is stalled on app chrome or many speculative mockups.
principles.exceptions: This is not a ban on up-front information architecture, journey modeling or approved navigation. Grayscale and paper are optional tools; low fidelity is useful only while it answers the question.

verification.question: Does the slice complete a useful task, and are consequential cross-feature dependencies still represented?

principles.title: Compare bounded choices in the real component

source.heading: RU-02 — Compare bounded choices in the real component

triggers: Spacing, sizing or token choices are drifting through nearly indistinguishable adjustments.
principles.exceptions: The sample base size, progression and approximate percentage step are examples, not invariants. Reuse the approved system; do not impose a new grid, prohibit fractional values, or require a complete token library before work begins.

verification.question: Can the selected value be explained by its role and compared in context, rather than by an arbitrary pixel nudge?

principles.title: Rebalance competing visual weight before enlarging the focus

source.heading: RU-03 — Rebalance competing visual weight before enlarging the focus

triggers: The main task loses attention despite large type, or icons and surfaces overpower adjacent content.
principles.exceptions: Supporting content still needs contrast, readability and discoverability. Required control boundaries cannot disappear. The book’s claim that icon weight cannot be changed is not universal; style families and native symbols may provide weight variants.

verification.question: Does the task become clearer while supporting content and control states remain readable and recognizable?

principles.title: Separate visual prominence from semantic structure

source.heading: RU-04 — Separate visual prominence from semantic structure

triggers: Utility headings, label/value pairs or destructive actions dominate solely because of their type.
principles.exceptions: Do not remove persistent form labels, units, periods, distinguishing terms or important visible headings. A quiet destructive entry still needs intelligible meaning and risk-appropriate handling; the example confirmation is not mandatory for every reversible action. Equally valid choices must not be hidden.

verification.question: Can a reader find the relevant field and understand its meaning, and can assistive navigation still identify headings and actions?

principles.title: Size content constraints and responsive proportions independently

source.heading: RU-05 — Size content constraints and responsive proportions independently

triggers: A form stretches across a wide viewport, a sidebar changes impractically, or a mobile view is a uniformly shrunk desktop.
principles.exceptions: The grid critique is not a prohibition on CSS Grid. The relative-sizing critique is not a ban on rem/em, fluid layout or user text scaling. Fixed widths must yield to available space and content. Generous whitespace is a starting exploration; dense comparison may be appropriate.

verification.question: Do the layout and relationships survive intermediate widths, longer strings and enlarged text without shrinking necessary copy or targets?

principles.title: Fit typography scales to actual roles and font behavior

source.heading: RU-06 — Fit typography scales to actual roles and font behavior

triggers: A geometric type scale skips a needed UI role or nested components produce unintended text sizes.
principles.exceptions: No mandatory font weight count, geometric ratio, integer size, Latin line-length range or system font stack. Parent-relative units can compound but are not prohibited. Optical tracking and tight heading leading must preserve scripts, accents and enlarged text. Quiet links still need persistent discoverability and focus behavior.

verification.question: Do the chosen roles render as intended with actual fonts, nested contexts, supported languages and text scaling?

principles.title: Construct color ramps through real component roles

source.heading: RU-07 — Construct color ramps through real component roles

triggers: A brand palette lacks useful text, surface, border or interaction-state shades.
principles.exceptions: Palette counts and hue-rotation limits are examples. HSL is an editing aid, not a required format or perceptual/compliance model. The brightness formula on pp. 153–154 is not WCAG relative luminance. Do not forbid true black, recolor meaningful categories, or replace approved color tooling.

verification.question: Do the light, middle and dark choices solve actual component roles across states rather than only form an attractive swatch strip?

principles.title: Reconcile readable contrast with secondary emphasis

source.heading: RU-08 — Reconcile readable contrast with secondary emphasis

triggers: A secondary colored badge becomes dominant, or muted text fails on a colored surface.
principles.exceptions: The p. 162 approximation of an 18px large-text boundary is inaccurate. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 uses 18pt regular or 14pt bold (or equivalent); apply the project’s current requirements and exceptions. Sample ratios and hue shifts are not reusable guarantees. Lightness differences can be useful cues, but the chart illustration does not establish accessible category mapping.

verification.question: Can secondary information remain readable while yielding attention to the primary task, with meaningful distinctions independently understandable?

principles.title: Make visual depth agree with layer order and state

source.heading: RU-09 — Make visual depth agree with layer order and state

triggers: A shadow looks muddy or arbitrary, or raised/inset styling conflicts with interaction state.
principles.exceptions: No mandatory light direction, five-shadow scale or photorealistic rendering. Preserve native materials and project conventions. Depth does not supply accessible state semantics or prove behavior; overlap must not obscure controls, focus or essential content.

verification.question: Do visual elevation and actual state agree, with coherent layer order and unobscured content in supported appearances?

principles.title: Validate image text contrast across local variation

source.heading: RU-10 — Validate image text contrast across local variation

triggers: Text overlays a photograph, a variable crop or user imagery.
principles.exceptions: An overlay, global tint, glow or shadow is only a candidate treatment, not contrast proof. Preserve faithful evidence/product imagery; do not recolor it just to match a brand. Decorative photography cannot substitute for explanatory content.

verification.question: Is text readable over the actual worst relevant crop and wrapping, including missing or changed images?

principles.title: Choose image detail and framing for actual rendered use

source.heading: RU-11 — Choose image detail and framing for actual rendered use

triggers: An optical asset-size mismatch makes a sharp vector look coarse when enlarged, a screenshot loses detail, or an upload crop loses meaning or breaks visual framing.
principles.exceptions: Do not reduce hit targets to match small glyphs, crop meaningful logos/diagrams indiscriminately, or universally convert semantic images to CSS backgrounds. An illustrative reconstruction is not a capture of shipped behavior. Use size-aware scalable families where they fit; the book’s pixel examples are not limits.

verification.question: Do key details and subjects survive the actual display size and varied uploads, with honest representation and appropriate fallback?

principles.title: Refine component composition without losing its task contract

source.heading: RU-12 — Refine component composition without losing its task contract

triggers: Default menus, table cells with independent sorting, or empty-state fixtures restrict a useful composition.
principles.exceptions: Custom appearance must retain keyboard, focus, selection and assistive behavior. A rich navigation popover is not automatically an ARIA menu. Do not hide filters needed to recover results or invite creation without permission. Border removal is optional when other cues preserve boundaries and grouping.

verification.question: Does the refined component retain its sorting/comparison/selection contract, and does each empty cause offer an appropriate next action?
